stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Excavators at the Bronze Age city of Ebla uncovered a palace archive containing thousands of broken clay tablets, and scholars have spent decades piecing the fragments back together. Each of the restored tablets, which record matters ranging from textile deliveries to diplomatic agreements with distant kingdoms, carries a small seal impression near ______ lower edge, a detail that has helped researchers identify individual scribes.
explanation: Cross out the prepositional phrase "of the restored tablets" and the relative clause, and the subject left standing is "Each". "Each" is always singular, and the lower edge belongs to a single tablet, so you need the singular possessive determiner "its".

A.why: You matched the pronoun to "tablets" or "kingdoms", plural nouns that sit near the blank. The real antecedent is "Each", which is singular, so the plural "their" does not agree with it.

C.why: "It's" means "it is", so the phrase becomes "near it is lower edge", which puts a verb where a possessive is needed. It sounds right read aloud, but it is a contraction, not a possessive.

D.why: "They're" means "they are", so the phrase becomes "near they are lower edge". That inserts a verb where a possessive belongs, and the pronoun is also plural when the antecedent "Each" is singular.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In 2021 the city of Marrowford replaced a zoning code that had governed construction since the 1960s. The new code, drafted after two years of public meetings with residents, business owners, and neighborhood associations, is best known for ______ elimination of minimum parking requirements near transit stops. Within three years, developers had converted several underused downtown garages into apartments.
explanation: The subject of the sentence is "The new code". The long participial phrase that follows it is an interrupter. It was the code that eliminated the parking requirements, so the blank needs a singular possessive, and that is "its".

A.why: "It's" is short for "it is", which gives you "best known for it is elimination". It sounds like the possessive, but it adds a verb where a determiner belongs.

B.why: You attached the pronoun to "neighborhood associations" or "business owners", the plural nouns closest to the blank. The noun that is known for the elimination is "The new code", which is singular, so "their" does not agree with it.

D.why: "There" names a place and cannot show possession. "Best known for there elimination" does not say whose elimination it was.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Labor economist Rhea Castellan spent two years tracking how a statewide minimum-wage increase affected small restaurants. Many analysts had predicted widespread layoffs. The restaurants in her sample, most of which were family-owned businesses employing fewer than ten workers, generally did not reduce their staff after the increase; instead, ______ raised menu prices slightly and cut back on overtime shifts.
explanation: The noun that raised prices and cut overtime is "The restaurants", the subject of the first clause. It is plural and names things, not a person, so the right pronoun is "they".

B.why: You matched the pronoun to "the increase", the singular noun right before the semicolon. An increase cannot raise menu prices. The restaurants did that, and "restaurants" is plural.

C.why: "She" refers to Castellan, but the passage presents her as the researcher who studied the restaurants, not the one who set their prices. This choice gives the restaurants' actions to the wrong person.

D.why: "This" is singular and does not clearly point to anything, so it cannot stand in for the plural noun "restaurants" that does the raising and cutting.

rated_why: identify plural subject to pronoun agreement

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Basque, spoken in communities along both sides of the border between Spain and France, has long puzzled historical linguists. Unlike its neighbors Spanish and French, both of which descend from Latin, Basque is classified as a language isolate: despite more than a century of comparative study, researchers have found no convincing evidence that ______ shared a common ancestor with any other living language.
explanation: The sentence is about Basque. It is the language classified as an isolate, so it is the thing that has no known relatives. "Basque" is singular and not a person, so the right pronoun is "it".

A.why: You matched the pronoun to "Spanish and French", the plural pair that sits between the antecedent and the blank. Those languages do have a known ancestor. The language with no relatives is Basque, which is singular.

B.why: "Them" is an object pronoun, but the blank is the subject of "shared". It is also plural, while "Basque" is singular.

C.why: "She" is a pronoun for a person. It cannot refer to a language, and the passage mentions no woman it could refer to.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Most of what we eat is broken down and absorbed long before it reaches the large intestine. Dietary fiber, unlike the proteins and fats that enzymes in the small intestine readily digest, passes into the colon largely intact. There, ______ can serve as food for trillions of resident bacteria, which ferment it into short-chain fatty acids that help nourish the cells lining the gut.
explanation: The thing that reaches the colon is "Dietary fiber", the subject of the previous sentence, and the later phrase "ferment it" confirms that it is singular. Fiber is singular and not a person, so the right pronoun is "it".

A.why: You matched the pronoun to "the proteins and fats", the plural nouns in the interrupter. The passage says those are digested in the small intestine and never reach the colon. The antecedent is "Dietary fiber", which is singular.

C.why: "These" is plural, so it points back to "proteins and fats" rather than to the singular "fiber". It also makes the passage contradict itself, because those nutrients are absorbed before the colon.

D.why: "Them" is an object pronoun, but the blank is the subject of "can serve". It is also plural, while the antecedent "fiber" is singular.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: To compare stroke technique across skill levels, sports scientists asked twelve collegiate athletes to complete timed trials on a single rowing ergometer. The machine, a model favored by many national-team coaches, was selected because ______ flywheel records the force of every stroke, allowing the researchers to detect subtle differences between novice and experienced rowers.
explanation: The thing with a flywheel is "The machine", the subject of the sentence. The phrase about the coaches is only an appositive between the subject and the verb. "Machine" is singular, so the possessive you need is "its".

B.why: "It's" means "it is", so the clause becomes "because it is flywheel records". It sounds like the possessive, but it adds a verb where a determiner belongs.

C.why: You matched the pronoun to "coaches", the plural noun in the appositive just before the blank. Coaches do not have a flywheel. The machine does, and "machine" is singular.

D.why: "They're" means "they are", which puts a verb where a possessive is needed. It is also plural, while the antecedent "machine" is singular.

rated_why: distinguish possessive its from contraction it's

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Provincial health officials faced a practical obstacle when planning vaccination drives in remote mountain villages. The vaccine they intended to distribute, unlike the oral drops used in earlier campaigns, loses ______ potency if it is stored above 8°C for more than a few hours. Health workers therefore carried the doses along mountain trails in solar-powered coolers.
explanation: The subject of the clause is "The vaccine". The phrase about the oral drops is an interrupter. It is the vaccine that loses potency when it gets warm, and the later "if it is stored" confirms that the antecedent is singular. The singular possessive you need is "its".

A.why: You matched the pronoun to "the oral drops" or "earlier campaigns", plural nouns that come right before the blank. The noun that loses potency is "The vaccine", which is singular, so "their" does not agree with it.

B.why: "It's" is short for "it is", which gives you "loses it is potency". It sounds right read aloud, but it adds a verb where a possessive belongs.

D.why: "They're" means "they are", so it cannot serve as a possessive. It is also plural, while the antecedent "vaccine" is singular.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Farmers who plant cover crops between cash-crop seasons often report firmer, less erosion-prone fields. Among cover crops, crimson clover is especially prized by growers of corn and wheat: like peas, beans, and other legumes, ______ can host bacteria in its roots that convert nitrogen from the air into a form that the following season's crops can absorb.
explanation: The sentence is about "crimson clover", the subject of the main clause before the colon, and the later phrase "in its roots" confirms that the antecedent is singular. Clover is a singular thing, not a person, so the right pronoun is "it".

A.why: You matched the pronoun to "peas, beans, and other legumes", the plural list right before the blank. That list is only a comparison. The subject is "crimson clover", which is singular, as "its roots" confirms.

B.why: "Them" is an object pronoun, but the blank is the subject of "can host". It is also plural, while "clover" is singular.

C.why: "One" is a generic pronoun for a person, so the sentence would say that some unnamed person hosts bacteria in its roots. The thing with roots and bacteria is the clover.
